newsitem.title: LEBANON: Workers at Lebanon public utilities on strike.
newsitem.headline: Workers at Lebanon public utilities on strike.

text.p: Lebanese workers at Beirut port and several other public utilities staged a one-day strike on Thursday to pressure the government to meet their pay demands.
Some 27,500 employees in public transportation, water and electricity utilities took part in the strike which paralysed activities at Beirut port, Lebanon's main export-import gateway.
The strike did not affect water and power supply across Lebanon.
"All 2,500 port employees and some 27,500 from other utilities took part in the strike," Antoine Bshara, head of the union of public utilities employees, told Reuters.
"This strike is intended as a warning to the government to meet the long-standing demands related to pay increases and promotions," Bshara added.
He said a 20 percent wage increase granted by the government to public sector employees last year has not officially become part of the workers' salaries.
"We're still taking this increase in the form of a grant rather than an actual pay rise. We want it to be officially part of our wages," Bshara said.
